newsitem.title: GERMANY: German industrial orders rise slightly in February.
newsitem.headline: German industrial orders rise slightly in February.

text.p: German industrial orders rose only slightly month-on-month in February but showed increasing momentum compared a year earlier, the Economics Ministry said on Thursday.
February's pan-German orders edged up 0.2 percent from January, but rose 6.2 percent compared to the year-ago period, according to preliminary data released by the ministry.

The main lift came from eastern Germany, where orders rose 4.9 percent month-on-month and 8.6 percent year-on-year. West German orders slipped 0.2 percent month-on-month but were still up 5.8 percent year-on-year.
The west German decline stemmed largely from a drop in foreign orders, which fell 2.3 percent after an unusually strong wave of foreign orders in January.
For the first two months of 1997, pan-German foreign orders were up 10.1 percent compared to the same period from 1996, the ministry said.

West German domestic orders, which had been dampened by Germany's weak economy, rebounded by 1.2 percent month-on-month in February in a move the ministry called "satisfying". For the January/February period, west German domestic orders were down 0.7 percent year-on-year.

Pan-German orders for intermediate goods also showed improvement in February, rising 2.6 percent month-on-month. For the January/February period, intermediate goods orders were up 5.5 percent compared to the same months in 1996.
Capital goods orders fell 2.7 percent month-on-month in February, but the total for February and January was up 2.1 percent year-on-year.
Orders for consumer goods and durables remained weak, falling 0.6 percent month-on-month in February. For the February/January period, they were up 0.5 percent compared to the year-ago period.
